# Fixture corpus

Real captures from a real World of Warcraft install, plus small recorded
responses from wago.tools. **No constructed examples here.** Constructed
inputs are allowed only for hostile-input and boundary tests, live inside
the test that uses them, and are labelled `constructed` (invariant L8).

## Rules

- **Capture tool only.** Every install file arrives through
  `scripts/lab_capture.py` (ticket M10-02), which replaces account folder
  names (and any `--extra-name`) with stable pseudonyms, rewrites the
  owner's own `Player-<n>-<hex>` GUIDs, blanks identity CVars, and refuses
  to emit a file that still contains an email address, a BattleTag, a home
  path carrying a login (since 2026-10-17, M13-49) or an unmapped
  `Player-<n>-<hex>` GUID. The home-path check fails closed: a URL path
  such as `https://example.org/home/page`, or a folder named `Users` or
  `Home` inside a path, refuses the file too. The repository is public; an
  unscrubbed capture is a leak.
  *Amended 2026-10-17 (M13-49, ADR-0019 amendment):* character names, realm
  names and the Forever second name are visible to anyone in the game, so
  they are no longer identifiers here: a new capture keeps them as they
  are, in paths and in contents, and a fixture, test, doc or PR may name
  them. Fixtures committed before this date keep their `Labchar…` and
  `Labrealm…` pseudonyms and their provenance rows; nothing is re-captured
  or edited.
- **Nothing else is edited.** Structure, key order, number text, escapes and
  line endings stay byte for byte. `.gitattributes` turns off end-of-line
  conversion for this directory.
- **Provenance.** Every file has a row below. A file without a row, or a row
  without a file, fails `make test-parser`.
- **Consent.** `owner` for the repository owner's own install; `explicit`
  for a file from anyone else's.
- **Staging.** Raw captures land in `incoming/` (gitignored). Review them,
  move them to `<platform>/<flavor-kind>/`, then add the rows. Never commit
  from `incoming/`.
- **One run per top-level folder** (2026-09-29, M11-23). A top-level
  folder is one capture run of one platform, laid out as an install root.
  A second run on a new build gets its own `<platform>-<build>` folder
  (`macos-70058/`), with that run's `.build.info` and `.flavor.info`, so a
  file whose path an earlier run already holds never replaces it. Earlier
  runs are never overwritten. The `platform` column stays the platform
  (`macos`), not the folder name.
  *Amended 2026-10-16 (M13-05), files-only runs.* A run folder may hold
  only the files a ticket needs, with no `.build.info` and no
  `.flavor.info`. It is then not an install root.
  - It must be declared, with its reason, in `FILES_ONLY_RUNS` in
    `tests/parser/test_layout_fixtures.py`. A test fails on an undeclared
    one.
  - It may hold SavedVariables files only.
  - Its `client_version` column comes from the capture run.
  - Its files are classified inside an install root borrowed from
    `macos/`.

  The first is `macos-70425/`, two `WowLab.lua` files. Its `.build.info`
  was left out for privacy: the tags cell carries a geo-IP country tag
  that `scripts/lab_capture.py` does not scrub (scrub rule: M13-34). Its
  `.flavor.info` was left out too. The staged copy is byte-identical to
  the committed `macos/forever/.flavor.info` (checked with `cmp`), so it
  adds nothing, and on its own it is no install root.
- **Immutability.** Never edit a committed fixture. A new client version is
  a new file.
- **Not fixtures.** Blizzard's exported interface code and art are never
  committed.
- **wago.tools recordings** go under `wago/`, with the URL and capture date
  in `edge_cases`. A whole recording is a public copy of the table, and the
  source's terms say do not mirror tables publicly (`docs/DATA_SOURCES.md`),
  so a table is recorded whole only when it is small and a test reads it
  whole (`docs/LAB_PLAN.md` §14.5 D4 and §14.6); everything else is a
  subset. A whole table has kind `wago-csv` and is named
  `<Table>.<build>.csv` as wago names the download. A table that is large,
  or that the repository has no reason to hold whole, is recorded as an
  **ID-filtered subset** (2026-09-30, M12-01, `docs/LAB_PLAN.md` §14.6): the
  header line and the whole, verbatim lines whose value in one named column
  is in a given set, in the download's order, cut by
  `scripts/wago_subset.py`, which copies lines byte for byte, never parses
  and re-serializes, and refuses a download whose SHA-256 is not the one
  given. A subset is named `<Table>.<build>.subset.csv` (it is not what wago
  sent) and has kind `wago-csv-subset`; its row states the full download's
  URL, date, size and SHA-256 (the download itself is not committed), the
  column, where the id set came from, and the counts the tool prints: values,
  lines kept of the download's lines, and the values that matched no line.
  An error response is recorded as its body only; cookies are never
  committed.
- **Addon managers' records** (2026-11-23, M22-16) go under
  `wowup/<platform>/`. They live outside any install (WowUp's user-data
  folder), so `scripts/lab_capture.py`, which takes an install root, cannot
  take them (a single-file mode is a later ticket), and
  `tests/parser/test_layout_fixtures.py` leaves `wowup/` out of the
  captured tree. The two so far were copied by hand, read only, after a
  search for tokens, keys, secrets, email addresses and home paths, and
  the capture tool's own detectors, run over each copy, found nothing but
  `/Users/Shared` (Battle.net's shared folder, no login), which is kept.
  Each copy was made by a one-off script that edits bytes and never parses
  and re-serializes; the edits are listed in the row's `scrub` cell, and
  nothing else is changed. WowUp's `sensitive.json` is never read or
  copied; the conductor accepted this hand copy as a one-off (2026-11-23).
  *2026-11-24 (M22-25):* every later file from outside an install goes
  through the capture tool's single-file mode, `scripts/lab_capture.py
  --file <path> --source <folder>`, which runs the install mode's detectors
  and refusals, blanks per-user link tokens, replaces app and account ids
  and this machine's home folder byte for byte, and writes the row, whose
  flavor cell says `n/a (outside an install)`. CurseForge's records go under
  `curseforge/<platform>/`; `test_layout_fixtures.py` leaves that folder
  out of the captured tree too.
- **Derived fixtures** (2026-10-19, M15-03; ADR-0033, L8's exception for
  asset formats). For the install's archives (the build config, the CASC
  index, encoding and root files, BLTE, M2 and skin, BLP) no byte of the
  real file is committed. `scripts/casc_facts.py` opens the install
  read-only and writes a JSON record of what was read from it: counts,
  versions, stored hashes, header facts and a handful of decoded rows.
  A derived fixture sits in its build's run folder under `derived/`
  (`macos-70450/derived/casc-index.json`) and its kind ends in `-derived`.
  It is not an install file: `tests/parser/test_layout_fixtures.py` leaves
  it out of the captured tree, so a run folder holding only derived
  fixtures is not a files-only run. Its `scrub` cell says what the record
  leaves out. Beside `casc-index.json`, `macos-70450/derived/dressing-room.json`
  (M15-02) records two outside dressing-room addresses the site's own
  encoder made for this run's characters, the inputs they were made from
  and what the site showed when it opened them, and
  `macos-70450/derived/casc-blte.json` (M15-04) records a few archive
  records' headers, chunk tables and decoded MD5s and a census of block
  modes across the local index, written by `scripts/casc_facts.py --blte`;
  `macos-70450/derived/casc-files.json` (M15-05) records the encoding and
  root files' facts, a census of the root against the local index, a
  handful of file data ids with their state and hashes, a ModelFileData
  sample's split into §17.1's states and the open's and reads' timings,
  written by `scripts/casc_facts.py --files`.
  `macos-70959/derived/m2-models.json` (M15-08) records two body models
  and their skins as `wowlab_core.m2` read them (counts, ids, chunk tags,
  texture types, geoset ids, header facts and triangle-edge means; no
  bytes, no hashes), written by `scripts/casc_facts.py --m2`.
  `macos-71037/derived/hotfix-items.json` (M22-23, under ADR-0033's note
  of 2026-11-23) records the client's hotfix cache, `DBCache.bin`: header,
  counts by table and status, and six items' records and rows, written by
  `scripts/hotfix_facts.py`. `wowsims/` holds the few entries of
  wowsims/forever's (MIT) item database the derived rows are checked
  against, values unchanged, with the commit and hash in the row.

Runbook for the owner's capture: `docs/handoffs/M10-03.md`.

## Columns

`file` is the path relative to this directory. `kind` is the format
(`build-info`, `flavor-info`, `savedvariables`, `config-wtf`, `bindings`,
`macros`, `toc`, `combatlog`, `wago-csv`, …). `flavor` is the flavor folder
as found on disk. `client_version` is the full version string from
`.build.info`. `platform` is the client that last wrote the file (`macos`,
`windows`), not the machine the capture ran on: it is there to explain line
endings and path spelling, so a capture made under Wine/Proton or from a
mounted drive must pass `--platform`. `scrub` records what the tool rewrote,
as it prints it: `identity-rewritten: n` (or `path only`), `cvars-blanked: n`,
`guids-rewritten: n`, `unit-guids-rewritten: n`,
`other-players-pseudonymised: n`, `timestamps-shifted`, `embedded: n`,
joined with `; `, or `none`. *Amended 2026-10-17 (M13-49):* from this
date `identity-rewritten: n` counts only rewrites of the account folder and
`--extra-name` strings, and `path only` means only the account or the
digits group folder was rewritten in the path; before it, both also counted
character and realm names. Rows from before and after the date do not
compare on this cell. *Amended 2026-10-18 (M13-55):* it also counts
rewrites of the `accountName` value found in a config file. The tool
prints each row ready to paste. Run it with
`--kind <flavor folder>=<flavor-kind>` and the `file` cell is already the
final path: move `incoming/<platform>/` up one level and the rows match.

What the scrub leaves behind is an artefact of the scrub, not evidence about
the client:

- A blanked line (`SET accountName ""`) says only that the CVar exists and
  how its line is shaped. It is not evidence that the client writes empty
  values.
- Pseudonyms (`Labchara`, `Labrealma Partb`, `90000001#1`,
  `Player-9999-00000001`) keep the real name's spaces, hyphens and
  apostrophes, so the relation between a realm's folder spelling and its
  normalised spellings survives. Their length, letters and casing pattern
  are invented, and they are always ASCII: a non-ASCII name becomes an ASCII
  pseudonym, so an ASCII name in a fixture says nothing about the real one.
  Non-ASCII coverage comes from the `non-ASCII strings` SavedVariables pick,
  a note that is only given to a file that still has such bytes after the
  scrub.
  The Forever second name gets a realm-style pseudonym (`Labrealm…`, as in
  `Labcharb-Labrealmd`) although it is not a realm (`docs/GLOSSARY.md`,
  Second name).
  Pseudonyms are stable within one capture run only: the tool assigns them
  in sorted order of the real names over the whole install, so part 1
  (`Labcharb-Labrealmd`) and part 2 (`Labchard-Labrealme`) are two runs and
  a pseudonym in one is not proven to mean the same real name in the other.
  Part 3 is a third run (build 70009): its log and `DBM-Party-Vanilla.lua`
  use its own spellings (`Labchard`, `Labrealmg`, `LabrealmbPartbPartcPartd`),
  which prove nothing about parts 1 and 2.
  The M11-03 lab-addon capture (build 70009, 2026-09-28) is a fourth run,
  re-run once with `--reuse-out` for a second character and the same
  identity map, so its two character folders `1/Labchard-Labrealmg` and
  `1/Labcharb-Labrealmf` are two different characters of one run. Each
  holds only the lab-addon's `WowLab.lua` in this tree. `Labcharb` here is
  not proven to be part 1's `Labcharb-Labrealmd`. Likewise `Labchard`:
  `layout` matches twins by first name only, so it now pairs
  `1/Labchard-Labrealmg` (this run, 70009) with
  `Labrealmb Partb Partc Partd/Labchard` (the `AddOns.txt` of part 2, 69977).
  Names from different runs are not proven to be the same character, so no
  test may rely on that pairing. The addon writes no names,
  so the three `WowLab.lua` files carry pseudonyms in their path only.
  The M11-23 capture (build 70058, 2026-09-29) is a fifth run, kept in its
  own install root `macos-70058/`. Its one character file sits at the same
  path as M11-03's `1/Labchard-Labrealmg/SavedVariables/WowLab.lua`.
  The capture notes say it is the same character after a barber-shop
  visit. Pseudonyms from different runs still prove nothing, so no test
  relies on the two files being one character.
  The M13-05 capture (build 70425, 2026-10-16) is a sixth run, kept in its
  own folder `macos-70425/`. It is the first schema-3 lab-addon capture,
  and the M11-29 barber-shop check rode along in the same session. Only its
  two `WowLab.lua` files are committed (conductor's ruling): no
  `.build.info` or `.flavor.info`, so `macos-70425/` is not an install
  root, and the install-discovery tests do not list it. Its character
  folder `1/Labchard-Labrealme` is this run's pseudonym. It is not proven
  to be M11-03's or M11-23's `Labchard`.
  The M15-01 captures (build 70450, 2026-10-19) are a seventh run: two
  runs of `scripts/lab_capture.py` by the owner on one day and build, one
  per character, kept together in `macos-70450/` (files-only, laid out as
  `macos-70425/` and declared in `FILES_ONLY_RUNS`). They are the first
  schema-4 lab-addon captures. Only the three `WowLab.lua` files are
  committed: the account one (byte-identical between the two runs, as was
  every other account-level file except `Purist_GearJourney.lua`, which
  only the first run has) and one per character. The rest of each run
  (34 and 35 files: other addons' SavedVariables, the WTF caches, the
  addon TOCs, a combat log) is not needed by M15-01 and stays out.
  Character and realm names are kept as they are (2026-10-17 rule), so
  the folders `1/Dangling-Participle` and `1/Sangraal-Sett` are the real
  ones; no earlier run's pseudonym is claimed to be either. Both
  characters are of the first body type, so `UnitSex` 3 (the second body
  type, from memory) is still unobserved.
  The M18-01T capture (build 70938, 2026-11-14) is an eighth run, kept in
  `macos-70938/` (files-only, laid out as `macos-70425/` and declared in
  `FILES_ONLY_RUNS`). Only the two game files that hold a positional `nil`
  hole are committed: the character `Blizzard_AuctionHouseUI.lua` and the
  account `Blizzard_CombatLog.lua`. The account `Blizzard_AuctionHouseUI.lua`
  of the run has no hole and is not committed (build 70009's is). The
  account `Auctionator.lua`, which holds two holes back to back
  (`["default_quantities"]`, indices 5 and 6), was refused by the scrub tool
  ("email address", 54 matches inside one encoded price-database string) and
  is not committed; two holes in a row are graded on a constructed input
  until a capture of it passes the scrub.
  The M21-02 capture (build 71037, 2026-11-23) is a ninth run, kept in
  `macos-71037/` with its own `.build.info` and `.flavor.info`. Only those,
  `WTF/Config.wtf` (`SET portal "US"`) and the first 120 lines of one
  launch-client combat log are committed. The log names every other player
  in four parts, `"<First>-<Second>-<Realm>-<Region>"`; the capture tool
  has no mode that keeps other players' names and pseudonymises only their
  GUIDs, so `--pseudonymise-other-players` replaced each first name
  (`Labothera`, `Labotherb`, ...) and kept the second name, realm and
  region as written. At 200 or 300 lines the tool refused the log (a real
  first name also appeared outside a unit field), so the slice is 120 lines.
  M22-22 (2026-11-23) added a second log of that build,
  `WoWCombatLog-012427_232527.txt`: 50 whole lines cut byte for byte from
  one real log into a scratch copy of the install before the capture tool
  ran (the tool keeps only a log's first lines, and the line wanted, the
  Shadowfang Keep zone line, is the log's last), so that file's row names
  the lines and the real log's hash.
  The M22-01 capture (build 71037, 2026-11-23) is a tenth run, on the same
  build as M21-02's and kept in the same `macos-71037/` tree, beside its
  files (not files-only). Only the Spy addon's three files are committed:
  the account `Spy.lua` (`SpyDB`) and two characters' (`SpyPerCharDB`),
  taken in two runs of the tool (one per character, `--sv Spy.lua
  --confirm-free-text Spy.lua`), whose account files were byte-identical.
  Spy is a notes addon, so the tool asked for the confirmation; every
  string was read first: other players' names, guilds, races, classes,
  zones and sub-zones, the owner's own character names, and the Forever
  port's own diagnostic lines (`ForeverDebug`). Names are kept under
  ADR-0036's note of 2026-11-23. Each run's other files and its newest
  combat log (refused: unmapped player GUIDs) are not committed. The
  account folder (`LABACCOUNTA`) and the digits folder (`1`) are the
  tool's pseudonyms, as in every run; the character folders are the real
  ones.
- Combat logs from part 3 on are captured with shifted timestamps (M10-02
  follow-up 5, `timestamps-shifted`): every stamp and the file name moved by
  one secret offset per log, format kept, so neither the date nor the time
  of day in a combat-log fixture is real.
- In a combat log, the server, instance, zone and spawn parts of every
  non-player unit GUID (`Creature-0-1-0-2-<npc id>-0000000000`) are invented,
  numbered in order of first appearance, from 2026-09-24 on
  (`unit-guids-rewritten: n`). The type and the NPC or object id are real. A
  zero server, instance or zone field is kept; a spawn UID is always
  renumbered. Equal invented values mean equal real values within one run
  only; the numbers themselves say nothing about the server, zone or spawn
  time.
- From 2026-09-24 on, a combat log's timestamps and the date in its file
  name are moved by a secret offset drawn for that log alone
  (`timestamps-shifted`). Every shifted timestamp is written in one fixed
  shape, `M/D/YYYY HH:MM:SS`, with the milliseconds and the UTC-offset suffix
  copied as written. That shape was verified on 2026-09-24 against the
  owner's real logs (count-only check). The time of day and the exact date are not the
  session's. The date is still bounded by the build's live window and by the
  commit date. The suffix still shows whether the session was in
  daylight-saving time. Durations and the order of events within a log are
  real.
- `embedded: n` counts replacements that touched a neighbouring letter or
  digit (a character named like the start of a longer word). Read those
  lines before trusting the file's vocabulary. CVar names and TOC directive
  keys are never rewritten.
